openings.claim: Existing lot-by-shift records may distinguish causes: a lot account predicts persistence across shifts; a process account predicts persistence across lots within the implicated shift.
openings.discriminator: Comparable crossed cells showing the opposite pattern defeat each prediction; confounded coverage cannot discriminate.
openings.probe: Inspect coverage and anonymous shift-level summaries using existing records, keeping missing values and absent cells unimputed.
openings.uncertainty: Crossed coverage and comparability are unknown. These are synthetic proposals, with no production records, measured defect rates, or causal findings supplied; non-identifiability remains possible.

openings.claim: New deliberately crossed samples could expose differences hidden by existing lot-shift assignments and reduce confounding.
openings.discriminator: Predicts better separability, without selecting a winning cause; continued inseparability defeats its proposed advantage.
openings.probe: Consider only after explicitly relaxing existing-records-only and obtaining a sampling resource; preserve employee anonymity and missing values.
openings.uncertainty: No additional sampling budget is supplied; access, expense, and discriminatory yield are unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves competing causal predictions and the coverage-dependent discriminator.
Preserves a distinct conditional path requiring explicit constraint relaxation and resources.
Assumption-generated estimates violate unimputed missingness; apparent completeness does not defeat confounding. Imputation bias and ranking stability remain unknown.

decision: Start with D1 under all hard constraints: existing records only, no employee identity disclosure, and no missing-value imputation. Report non-identifiability if coverage is inadequate. D2 remains conditional on explicit relaxation and resources; no new sampling or imputation is authorized.
